page: Amazon Web Services c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and third-generation AMD EPYC 7R13 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a sustained clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The CPU features 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 8 MB L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AES, VAES, SHA-NI, AVX, and bit-manipulation extensions, while omitting AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets.

The configuration provides 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Networking throughput delivers a baseline rate of 2 Gbps. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring remote Amazon Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent disk storage operations and operating system deployments.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded compute output, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring in the top 25 percent. Single-thread data compression and Geekbench single-core execution maintain average ratings. However, multi-core throughput and memory subsystems demonstrate clear capacity limits. Overall Geekbench multi-core metrics, stress-ng multi-core testing, and PassMark memory benchmarks land in lower percentiles, constrained by the 4-vCPU footprint and moderate memory bandwidth.

The hardware profile delivers cost-effective processing for single-threaded tasks, distributed application nodes, batch processing, static web serving, and microservices requiring dedicated CPU cycles over expansive memory. Workloads dependent on wide vector instructions, high-bandwidth in-memory caching, or massive parallel databases may face throughput bottlenecks.

Amazon Web Services c6a.xlarge is suitable for containerized web services, CI/CD worker agents, modest data encoding jobs, and light caching tiers where consistent CPU clock rates take precedence over large RAM allocations.
description: Amazon Web Services c6a.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 7R13 processors clocked at 3.6 GHz. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, paired with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory at a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. The instance includes no local storage or hardware accelerators, depending on remote EBS volumes and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmark evaluations, the c6a.xlarge achieves strong single-core CPU execution while exhibiting lower ratings in multi-core metrics and memory bandwidth due to its 4-vCPU configuration. Cryptographic extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI enhance secure processing efficiency, though AVX-512 extensions are absent. The instance provides an economical solution for batch computing, CI/CD compilation, web servers, and containerized microservices requiring dedicated compute capabilities.
